draft.title: Types of business
card: Sole trader
one person owns the business. The owner has unlimited liability, so personal assets can be used to pay the business's debts.
Partnership
two or more people own the business and share its profits and risks. In a general partnership, each partner has unlimited liability.
Company

a separate legal entity owned by shareholders, who have limited liability. A private company's shares are not sold on the stock exchange. A public listed company's shares are traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX).
Social enterprise and GBE
a social enterprise is run for a social or environmental purpose. A government business enterprise (GBE) is owned by government and sells goods or services.
draft.remember: Types of business differ in who owns them, who is liable for debts, and what they aim to do.

a.q: Jai runs a gardening business alone. It cannot pay a large debt. What is his position as a sole trader?
opts: His personal assets can be used to pay the debt
His liability is limited to the money he put in
The business is a separate entity that alone owes the debt
Shareholders must share the debt with him
a.why: A sole trader has unlimited liability, so personal assets can be used to pay business debts. Limited liability applies to company shareholders, not sole traders.
a.clue: Is a sole trader separate from the business in law?

b.q: Lena and Tom want to open a bakery in Geelong. They want the owners' personal assets protected from business debts, and they want shares kept out of the stock exchange. Which type of business suits them?
opts: A private company
A public listed company
A general partnership
A sole trader
b.why: A private company gives shareholders limited liability, and its shares are not traded on the stock exchange. A public listed company also has limited liability, but its shares are traded on the ASX. A general partnership leaves partners with unlimited liability.
b.clue: Which type has limited liability and no stock exchange listing?

a.best: His personal assets can be used to pay the debt

proposal.title: Types of business
card: Sole trader
one person owns the business, and in law the owner and business are not separate. The owner has unlimited liability, so personal assets can be used to pay the business's debts.
Partnership
two or more people own the business and share its profits and risks. In a general partnership, each partner has unlimited liability.
Company

a separate legal entity owned by shareholders, who have limited liability. A private company's shares are not traded on the stock exchange. A public listed company's shares are traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX).
Aims also differ. Sole traders, partnerships and most companies aim to make a profit for their owners. Social enterprises and government business enterprises (GBEs) have other aims as well.
